Subject: Hosted API baseline + competitor comparison

Hi Jordan,

We're kicking off evaluation for a hosted LLM API provider to power our in-app search and recommendations across 300k monthly active users. Our procurement team asked me to collect baseline rate cards and any competitor benchmarking you can share. Specifically: 1) list of per-token rates (prompt/completion or equivalent), 2) embedding costs, 3) any volume tiers or committed discounts, and 4) SLOs for latency.

For context, we have competing quotes on the table:
- OpenAI: $0.03 per 1k prompt tokens / $0.06 per 1k completion tokens (mid-sized model); embedding $0.0004/vector at scale
- Anthropic: flat $X per 1k tokens (they quoted a blended rate, will share spreadsheet)
- Together: discounted bundles for committed spend
- AWS Bedrock: higher list price but enterprise credits and marketplace concessions

Can Redwood provide a formal baseline and tell us where you can be competitive vs. these vendors? Key timeline: procurement will shortlist vendors by 5/25 and we hope to finalize by mid-June.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Sam
Sam Connors
Senior Product Manager, Nova Retail
sam.connors@novaretail.com

Hi Sam — thanks for the note and the context.

We can absolutely put together a clear baseline and a short competitor comparison for your procurement team. I've attached our bundled hosted API rate card (redwood_hosted-ratecard-v1.pdf) and an internal one-page that highlights where Redwood typically outperforms the major vendors on cost-per-effective-token when customers use our KV caching and batching defaults.

Could you confirm expected monthly token volumes (prompt vs completion split) and a desired commit window (monthly vs 12/24 months)? That will let us model committed discounts vs on-demand. If you prefer, I can draft a candidate commercial that matches the OpenAI blended numbers you shared and include an incentive for a one-quarter pilot.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the volume split and the procurement spreadsheet (you mentioned a file)
- We send a formal quote and a 30-day pilot offer by 5/21
- Short call to walk the numbers (15–20m) if helpful

If that plan works I'll loop in Rachel (bd ops) for a formal quote.

Best,
Jordan

Jordan — thanks, attaching the procurement sheet (novaretail-competitor-quotes.xlsx). Key numbers below (monthly):
- Expected tokens: 2.5B total tokens / month (estimated 30% prompt / 70% completion)
- Embeddings: 1.2M vectors per month
- Current commercial pressure: Procurement is prioritizing unit cost and predictability over marginal latency differences.

Vendor quotes summarized in the sheet: OpenAI blended (~$0.045 per 1k tokens), Anthropic quoted $0.05 per 1k, Together gave a commit-based bundle (requires 6mo min), AWS Bedrock offered marketplace credit with a T&Cs caveat.

We'd like a Redwood commercial that:
1) matches or beats the OpenAI blended unit economics on baseline usage, and
2) includes a clear committed tier for predictable monthly price with automatic rollback to on-demand if we miss thresholds.

Procurement would like a PDF quote and any sample contract language around data residency and audit logs. Shortlisting deadline: COB 5/25.

Sam

Vanessa / Rachel — forwarding Sam's ask and the competitor sheet. Key ask: match or beat OpenAI blended at ~ $0.045 / 1k tokens for ~2.5B tokens/mo; embeddings ~1.2M vectors/mo. Procurement wants a PDF quote and sample contract language for data residency/audit logs. Shortlisting cob 5/25.

My read: we can structure a 12-month committed rate that nets to $0.038–0.042 per 1k tokens if we tier the commit and include KV caching defaults. That keeps gross margin but should be attractive vs. OpenAI. Proposed concessions to consider:
- 5% introductory credit for first 60 days (pilot)
- 8–12% committed discount on list if they sign 12 months and meet 80% of monthly target
- Embedding price: propose $0.00035/vector for 1.2M+ vol

Operational asks for the quote: SLA 99.9% uptime, latency SLOs documented per route, audit logs exported to their S3 (customer-managed), and SOC2 evidence pack. Legal will likely request a custom DPA and KMS integration notes.

Can you 1) confirm the pricing band above is acceptable, 2) suggest any commercial levers we should add (credits, onboarding discount, shorter pilot), and 3) if ok, Rachel can produce the formal PDF quote + sample terms by 5/21.

Thanks — Jordan

Thanks for the summary, Jordan. The pricing band you proposed is reasonable and defensible given our caching/optimizer delta. A few notes:

1) Approve: 12-month commit with graded tiers that yield $0.038–0.042 per 1k tokens at their projected volume. Include a 60-day pilot credit of 5% (applied to first two invoice runs) to accelerate procurement.
2) Embeddings: approve $0.00035/vector for 1.2M+ volume, with a floor for the first three months.
3) Commercial levers: add a one-time onboarding credit for integration assistance (up to $10k) instead of a further unit discount — preserves long-term unit economics and gives procurement a visible concession.
4) Legal/Privacy: Rachel, please include SOC2 attestation, sample DPA with KMS integration term sheet, and an exportable audit-log hook (S3 endpoint) in the sample terms. Also prep a short clause that states automatic rollback to on-demand rates if thresholds are missed for two consecutive months.

Jordan — have Rachel draft the PDF quote with those elements and run it by me for quick sign-off. If procurement pushes for parity with an unblended OpenAI enterprise deal, call that out as a negotiation point and keep the onboarding credit as our primary concession.

Vanessa
